system.description:
The Embrace deprives a Tremere of the ability to function as a magus, but it does not sever the bond formed with a familiar while the character was still mortal. Only characters who were mortal magi before their Embrace may take this Background. The bound spirit may take the form of a small animal traditionally associated with magi and witches — a cat, raven, mouse, or frog — or appear as a homunculus or mannikin; large animals such as horses or bears, and magical creatures such as dragons, are not available as familiars. Though it no longer serves precisely as a magus's familiar once did, it still performs simple tasks and minor guardianship duties, and it holds its master to whatever agreements were struck when it was first bound — a Tremere who reneges on those terms risks losing the creature's favor.

The dots invested determine the familiar's capability, with each rating including the benefits of all lower ratings: at the lowest rating it performs only minor services and will not risk itself; at the next it acts as an early warning of intruders without confronting them; further investment lets it perform complex tasks and act as a messenger, attempting (without directly engaging) to deter hostile creatures from the haven; and at its highest rating the familiar has developed a true fondness for its master despite his unliving state, acting as a genuine assistant willing to incur minor risk to its own form to protect him.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers (Tremere)
